title: One to five
goal: Count, read, write and order 1 to 5.
integration: Isolated candidate overlay; canonical lessons and existing edition remain unchanged until review.
setting: A fictional shaded school activity table in Gombe
story_dialogue: Oops! I counted that counter twice.
Touch each counter once. Say its number.
Slide it onto the mat. I'll check with you!
play: A partner shows 1 to 5 large counters. Count them. Choose the matching number card. Swap roles.

story_dialogue: Can you help us count our game pieces?
Let's put them in a line.
Say one number each time you touch one!
clarity_revision.worked_instruction: Start at the left. Touch the first dot and say 'one'.
clarity_revision.worked_say: Touch the next dot and say 'two'.
clarity_revision.worked_total: Touch the last dot and say 'three'.
clarity_revision.mistake_explanation: He gave the middle dot two numbers.
clarity_revision.fresh_check: Put 4 counters on the table for Grace.
clarity_revision.recognition_instruction: Ask a partner to say one number below. Point to it.

teacher_responses.notice: A dot is skipped or counted twice.
teacher_responses.try: Put counters in a line. Touch one while saying one number.
teacher_responses.recheck: Give a fresh set of 2, then 3. Watch each touch.

teacher_responses.notice: The child counts but cannot say how many.
teacher_responses.try: Repeat the last number: 'Three. There are three.'
teacher_responses.recheck: Count a fresh set and ask 'How many altogether?'

teacher_responses.notice: Numerals are copied but not recognised.
teacher_responses.try: Match a small set to its number card. Say the number.
teacher_responses.recheck: Shuffle the cards. Ask for 1, then 2, then 4.

story_dialogue: Let's count the counters for our game!
Move it onto the mat. We can check together!

teacher_responses.notice: A counter is skipped or counted twice.
teacher_responses.try: Move one counter onto the mat for each number said.
teacher_responses.recheck: Give a fresh set of 2, then 3. Watch each move.

teacher_responses.notice: The child counts but cannot say how many.
teacher_responses.try: Repeat the last number: 'Three. There are three.'
teacher_responses.recheck: Count a fresh set and ask 'How many altogether?'

teacher_responses.notice: Numerals are copied but not recognised.
teacher_responses.try: Match a small set to its number card. Say the number.
teacher_responses.recheck: Shuffle the cards. Ask for 1, then 2, then 4.

teaching_revision.later_check: Ask the child to give John 5 counters. Spread them out. Ask how many again. Offer the mat method if needed.

questions.prompt: Count row A. Write the number.
Count row B. Write the number.
Adamu counts one counter twice. Show a better way.
questions.answer: Touch or move each top exactly once.
